thesis: Even at the moment of public bara'ah, the passage commands believers to honor faithful treaty partners to term (9:4), confront those left outside any pact only after the revealed interval with a binding release upon repentance (9:5), and grant individual asylum plus safe escort to any seeker who asks to hear the Qur'an (9:6).

flags.quote: those who never had a pact, those who broke one, those whose fixed term has run out
flags.issue: Al-Tabari's three-part criterion at 9:5 reads 'عن الذين لا عهد لهم، أو عن الذين كان لهم عهد فنقضوا عهدهم بمظاهرتهم الأعداءَ ... أو كان عهدهم إلى أجل غيره معلوم' — the third category is a pact to an UNSPECIFIED term, not a fixed term that has expired. The load-bearing point (Tabari sets the boundary by treaty status, not by observed hostility) is verbatim correct; only the third label is loosely rendered, and it converges on the same class (outside any pact once the interval ends).

flags.quote: al-Tabari records that some held 9:6 abrogated as well — and rules against them
flags.issue: Source-segmentation caveat, not a fabrication. The fetched al-Tabari places the naskh discussion inside the 9:6 block: Ibn Zayd on ﴿ثم أبلغه مأمنه﴾ says 'وليس هذا بمنسوخ'; Tabari then opens 'واختلفت في حكم هذه الآية، وهل هو منسوخ أو هو غير منسوخ؟' and closes 'والصواب من القول في ذلك عندي، قولُ من قال: ليس ذلك بمنسوخ'. However, the reports the 'abrogated' camp adduces (ad-Dahhak, as-Suddi, Qatadah, athar 16487-16489) all concern ﴿فاقتلوا المشركين﴾ against 47:4, so strictly the tarjih may attach to 9:5's naskh relation rather than to 9:6's aman. Either way al-Tabari rejects abrogation and the asylum/escort command stands operative in his own tafsir of 9:6, so the file's practical claim holds.

notes: ORIGINAL FLAG RESOLVED. Every named attribution in the new section matches the fetched tafsir. Ibn Kathir DOES carry Ad-Dahhak ibn Muzahim verbatim: 'This honorable Ayah (9:5) was called the Ayah of the Sword, about which Ad-Dahhak bin Muzahim said, "It abrogated every agreement of peace between the Prophet and any idolator, every treaty, and every term." Al-'Awfi said that Ibn 'Abbas commented: "No idolator had any more treaty or promise of safety ever since Surah Bara'ah was revealed."' Al-Tabari DOES define the targets by treaty status at 9:5 (those with no pact / pact-breakers who backed enemies / term-class), not by behaviour. Al-Tabari DOES rule against abrogation in the 9:6 block ('ليس ذلك بمنسوخ') with Ibn Zayd's 'وليس هذا بمنسوخ' on the escort clause — see the second flag for the one caveat. 9:4 attribution checks in both editions (Ibn Kathir: treaties with a specific termination date 'lasted until its specific termination date'; Tabari: 'فَفُوا لهم بعهدهم ... ولا تنصبوا لهم حربًا إلى انقضاء أجل عهدهم'). The section reports the dispute without adjudicating it — Dahhak's position is called 'a real classical position, held by real authorities' that 'reads the verse far more broadly than this reflection does', with no move to refute it. Tadabbur-vs-fatwa line present and explicit ('None of this is a legal ruling ... For rulings, ask a qualified scholar'). The batch4 moderate flag on scope language is also addressed: both 'declared hostility' sentences (Introduction and the 9:5 section) were reworded to treaty-status language. Residual 'hostile' phrasing survives in later contemplative passages (lines 151, 247, 325), but it is now transparently framed rather than presented as the verse's own criterion. Downstream: the published /posts/quran-9-5-sword-verse-kill-the-unbelievers article rests on this file and should be checked for the same ikhtilaf paragraph.

thesis: When Allah and His Messenger sever a false covenant they do it with public clarity, a defined time span, and open warning, so that even hard judgment remains morally legible and repentance stays open.
notes: ORIGINAL FLAG RESOLVED. All three attributions in the new section verify against the fetched tafsir. (1) Al-Tabari does record several competing positions on whom the four months covered — 'فقال بعضهم' / 'وقال آخرون' recurs five times (two classes of treaty-holder; treaty-holders four months vs fifty nights for the pactless; one uniform term for all idolaters; al-Zuhri's Shawwal reckoning; al-Kalbi's sub-four-month restriction), matching the file's 'every idolater / open-ended pacts / those who had broken faith'. (2) Tabari's own tarjih is verbatim what the file claims: 'وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب ... إنما هو لأهل العهد الذين ظاهروا على رسول الله ﷺ، ونقضوا عهدهم قبل انقضاء مدته. فأما الذين لم ينقضوا عهدهم ولم يظاهروا عليه، فإن الله ... أمر نبيه بإتمام العهد ... بقوله ﴿فَأَتِمُّوا إِلَيْهِمْ عَهْدَهُمْ إِلَى مُدَّتِهِمْ﴾', reinforced by 'فأما من كان أجل عهده محدودًا ... كان بإتمام عهده إلى غاية أجله مأمورًا'. Ibn Kathir matches: 'As for those whose term of peace ended at a specific date later (than the four months), then their treaties would end when their terms ended, no matter how long afterwards, for Allah said (So fulfill their treaty for them until the end of their term)[9:4].' (3) The 'Arafah-vs-Nahr dispute is explicit: 'وأما قوله ﴿يوم الحج الأكبر﴾ فإنه فيه اختلافًا بين أهل العلم. فقال بعضهم: هو يوم عرفة' against 'وقال آخرون: هو يوم النحر'. Section reports without adjudicating (no camp preferred; Tabari's tarjih is reported as his, not endorsed as the answer), and the tadabbur-vs-fatwa line is present.

thesis: When fear of hostile people competes with fear of Allah, necessary struggle becomes a revelation of the heart, exposing whether fear is rightly ordered and where hidden loyalties (walijah) still live.

flags.quote: the breach of the Hudaybiyyah treaty when Banu Bakr moved against Khuza'ah under Quraysh's cover
flags.issue: Ibn Kathir's wording is 'the idolators breaking the peace agreement with Muslims and aiding Bani Bakr, their allies, against Khuza'ah, the ally of the Messenger of Allah' — he does not name Hudaybiyyah in this passage. The identification is standard and uncontested sirah, so this is a naming gloss rather than a claim mismatch.

flags.quote: although the ayah takes in all believers, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and as-Suddi read it as referring to Khuza'ah specifically
flags.issue: No issue — recorded here only to note it is a near-verbatim match with Ibn Kathir: 'This Ayah includes all believers, even though Mujahid, 'Ikrimah and As-Suddi said that it refers to Khuza'ah.' Listed for the human's trace, not as a defect.

notes: ORIGINAL FLAG RESOLVED. Both disputes the batch3 read said were omitted are now named with the right authorities and in Ibn Kathir's own order: the occasion ('(while they did attack you first), refers to the battle of Badr ... It was also said that these Ayat refer to the idolators breaking the peace agreement with Muslims and aiding Bani Bakr ... against Khuza'ah'), and the scope of 'heal the breasts of a believing people' (all believers vs Khuza'ah per Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, as-Suddi). The section explicitly declines to settle either dispute ('That reading does not depend on settling either dispute') and carries both a tadabbur-vs-fatwa line and the legitimate-authority condition the original flag asked for ('nothing here establishes when confrontation is warranted, or who decides it. Those are questions of fiqh with conditions of legitimate authority attached'). The two remaining batch3 minor flags (khashyah/khawf lexical over-claim; 'five verbs' where the fifth sits in 9:15) were not touched by this repair and are still open as minor items.
